messages:
maria.g: Hey people-ops — I had to go to an ER in Barcelona last night. Provider says they can bill my insurer directly but they want an 'EOB' in Spanish + an invoice with VAT number and IBAN. I paid up front. Can People Ops / benefits help with the right docs and an expedited proof of coverage for their billing desk? Also curious about reimbursement timeline. Thanks!

leo.benefits: Sorry to hear that, glad you’re ok! :heart: Quick checklist for international claims: itemized invoice (procedures/diagnosis or clear descriptions), proof of payment (card receipt or bank statement), provider name + tax/VAT id + bank/IBAN, and a translation if available. We can request an insurer EOB but they often issue EOBs in English. Did the hospital ask to bill insurer directly or just asked for an EOB copy?

maria.g: They said their accounting team will only process direct billing if we provide an insurer EOB and our policy contact — otherwise they want payment up front. They insist on invoice with VAT number + IBAN.

claims_bot: Automated claim note: To submit an international reimbursement, go to https://benefits.redwood.com/claims and select "International reimbursement." Accepted file types: pdf, jpg, png. Required: date of service, currency paid, total paid, proof of exchange rate (bank or OANDA screenshot). Typical processing time ~4–8 weeks.

leo.benefits: Useful email you can send to the provider (copy/paste):
```
Hi — I need an itemized invoice showing procedure/diagnosis descriptions, your tax/VAT ID, and bank details (IBAN) so I can request direct billing from my insurer. If possible please include an English translation of the invoice or a short English summary of line items. I will submit these documents to my insurer for processing. Thank you, Maria G.
```

sophia.hr: We can also generate a temporary proof-of-coverage letter (policy number + claim intake contact + short note authorizing provider to contact insurer) you can hand them. @leo.benefits can you produce an expedited PDF for Maria?

leo.benefits: Yep, I can. Maria — DM me a photo/scan of the invoice and the hospital billing contact and I’ll produce a letter with the insurer claim email/phone and a short cover note. I’ll aim to send within a few hours. Note: insurer may still ask for original receipts for reimbursement.

jon.claims: When you submit, include a currency conversion record for the date of service (OANDA or your card statement) and a clear itemized invoice. Insurers sometimes reimburse net of VAT — depends on policy. If the provider bills insurer directly, make sure they attach their invoice plus your authorization letter. I’ll flag this as an international claim to speed review.

maria.g: Awesome — one more Q: provider asked for a phone number to verify coverage in Spanish. Do we have a Spanish-speaking claims line?

leo.benefits: We’ll include the insurer’s multilingual claims phone number in the letter. They have limited Spanish support Mon–Fri 9–17 CET: +1-800-555-0199 (note: not guaranteed to be fully bilingual). I’ll add the claim intake email address too so they can email documents directly. :thumbsup:

sophia.hr: If direct billing falls through, submit for reimbursement via the portal and mark as "urgent" and attach travel dates / work trip proof (boarding pass or calendar invite). That sometimes speeds approval for business travel claims.

maria.g: Sending invoice and billing contact via DM now. Thanks so much for the quick help!!
